review_comments:
Importing them with a star means potentially bundling a lot of unused helpers. Having them named helps save some bytes.

It really is a two edged sword, like sometimes the whole re-importing text written dozens of times amounts to more space than caused by the unused helpers. Really depends on size of helpers and how much you think in a near-enough-to-worry-about future.

Babel went towards the named individually path, do you think it makes sense for swc to adopt the same pattern?
Babel's helper works in this way and module bundler with tree shaking can remove unused imports. So I'm not sure if importing only used stuffs is necessary.

I believe if '@swc/helpers' itself can be statically analyzed (only using es6 imports/exports) a bundler can do the needed tree shaking.  

Although I don't actually know which bundlers do and which don't do this...
